topics.topic_label: Tool-use & agent-UI standards (ScrambleToolBench strips the semantic cues out of tool schemas so agents must discover behaviour by interaction — and finds successful discovery does not transfer to robust adaptation; the MCP/A2A boundary drawn through division of labour rather than spec comparison)

Evaluation gap (execution, outcome and experience named as three different questions an agent can split on — a scheduler that books exactly as instructed but never confirms the timezone; Lyft had to make its simulated customers *worse* because articulate LLM users produced >90% offline pass rates that died in production; LATAM found 95% of 'out of scope' classifications were real needs)

Tool-use & agent-UI standards (SkillTrace makes skill composition an explicit graph traversal; the 28 July extensions framework lets Tasks and MCP Apps ship without touching a core that is now stateless; and the day's LinkedIn argument is that neither A2A nor MCP will supply the governance layer between them)

Evaluation gap (frontier science benchmarks are being passed by shortcut rather than reasoning, so headline scores overstate capability — which lands the same day as this week's automated-mathematics claims and a benchmark-saturation study on the HN front page; the eval-practice answer is that the bottleneck has moved from writing evals to stopping agents from grading their own homework)

Tool-use & interop standards (A2A passes 150 organisations with v1.0 stable and native integration across Google, Microsoft and AWS, while the decision framework doing the rounds names the actual trade - plain APIs when the caller knows what it wants, MCP when the model must discover capability at runtime, A2A when the counterparty is itself non-deterministic, and MCP buys discovery at the price of a much larger, less predictable trust surface)

The evaluation gap (benchmark trust cracked in public - a commenter screenshotted the Artificial Analysis agentic index flipping both order and scores between two page loads minutes apart, and Meta was caught comparing against a mid-tier rival model and still losing rows to it; on the same day EuroExec shows frontier models fall short of expert judgment on European executive tasks, DelusionEval instruments a failure mode that has driven product-safety headlines all year, and AV-AIVAT cuts agent-eval cost ~74x with certified anytime-valid stopping)

Tool-use & discovery standards (The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling applies a Sutton-style argument to tool use — hand-engineered tool schemas, routers and selection heuristics lose to scale and general learning, cutting directly against the tool-registry and description-engineering layers most MCP-era agent stacks are building; two practitioner pieces settle MCP-vs-A2A as division of labour, A2A for delegation and MCP for tools and data)

Evaluation gap (the sharpest item of the day is a reproducibility challenge — a commenter screenshots the Artificial Analysis agentic leaderboard flipping both order AND scores between two page loads minutes apart with identical chart copy, Qwen 55.4 vs Opus Max 55.3 then Opus Max 59.2 vs Qwen 58.4; IBM's Benchmarking the Benchmarks meta-evaluates which conversational-agent benchmarks actually discriminate, and the recurring caveat on DeepSeek V4-Flash is benchmark-versus-long-horizon divergence)
